heading.title: Of Mortgages of Immoveable Property and Charges

article.title: Mortgage when to be by assurance.
article.content:
59Mortgage when to be by assurance.

Section 59  ·  Chapter IV  ·  page 24 of the Act
Where the principal money secured is one hundred rupees or upwards, a mortgage 5[other than a mortgage by deposit of title-deeds] can be effected only by a registered instrument signed by the mortgagor and attested by at least two witnesses. Where the principal money secured is less than one hundred rupees, a mortgage may be effected either by 6[a registered instrument] signed and attested as aforesaid, or (except in the case of a simple mortgage) by delivery of the property.
7* * * *
5 Ins. by Act 20 of 1929, s. 20.
6 Subs. by Act 6 of 1904, s. 3, for “an instrument”.
7 Third paragraph omitted by Act 20 of 1929, s. 20.
